source: BK3 printed p.59 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.65; BK3 printed p.58 = PDF p.64 (error expressions); ERRATA ER-15 (prose only), ER-16 (diagram only); Step 7 speculative derivation from topology
note: Speculative (Step 7): every expect is derived by hand from the wiring and the p.59 rule (light 3 ON = error; slide switch LEFT = the positive condition). Slide-switch roles per jack-map: S/V arms, R/U close LEFT, T/W close RIGHT; switch target 0 = LEFT, 1000 = RIGHT. Nodes: P = {+, 2S, 3V}; A = {2T, 3S}; B = {2R, 1S}; D = {3U, 2V, 1V}; COM = {3com, 3T, 1T, 2W, 1W, 3A}; 1R, 1U, 2U, 3R, 3W unwired. Light 3 is lit exactly when P reaches COM: 2S-2T-3S-3T (S-bar x W-bar), 2S-2R-1S-1T (C-bar x S), 3V-3U-2V-2W or 3V-3U-2V/1V-1W (W x (S-bar + C-bar)). These are the three p.58 error expressions (ER-15 form for the second), with no sneak path: light 3 is off only with switches 1 and 2 LEFT (Camille could, Sara should), for either position of switch 3, which agrees with the p.59 note that a riddle can have more than one complete solution. The script sweeps all eight settings in Gray order from all-LEFT and returns to all-LEFT. Switches are set LEFT before power-on so the first state is not the simulator's default switch position. The 500 ms advance before each expect lets the lamp finish its thermal transient; the page states no timing.

script.cite: BK3 printed p.59 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.65, rule 'Light 3 ON represents an error' with slide switch LEFT = positive condition (1 Camille could, 2 Sara should, 3 Wanda would); error expressions BK3 p.58 (PDF p.64) S-bar x W-bar, C-bar x S (ER-15), W x (S-bar + C-bar); derived from topology: power ON, switches 1, 2, 3 all LEFT (C, S, W): switch 1 LEFT opens 1S-1T and 1V-1W, switch 2 LEFT opens 2S-2T and 2V-2W, so the only arm paths are 2S-2R-1S (dead at 1R) and, with switch 3 LEFT, 3V-3U-2V-1V (dead at 2U and 1U); nothing reaches 3com, light 3 off; no error expression is true
script.quote: Light 3 ON represents an error. ... If the power is ON and light 3 is OFF, slide switches 1, 2 and 3 are indicating a correct solution to the problem. (Note: for some logical riddles there is more than one complete solution)
